claims.result: Countable aggregation exactly adapts to each fixed class with finite divergent minimax KL benchmark.
claims.scope: Countable prescribed family; approximate minimax codes; no computability or projective consistency guarantee.

claims.result: For C_p={Bernoulli(p),Bernoulli(1-p)}, p in (0,1/2), minimax KL tends to ln 2. No single coding sequence achieves a finite class-dependent asymptotic factor for every C_p.
claims.scope: Two-point nondegenerate source classes, not envelope classes. Infinite limsup outside a countable set; not necessarily divergence to infinity.

claims.result: No countable coordinatewise-cofinal catalogue of nonnegative nonincreasing summable envelopes covers all admissible monotone summable envelopes.
claims.scope: Literal coordinatewise domination only; no impossibility for all coding methods or the regularly varying subclass.

claims.result: Power-tail and exponential benchmark integrations, fixed-exponent-grid limitation, and integer-prefix Kraft barrier.
claims.scope: No sharp positive-index minimax constant established. Kraft barrier does not imply necessity of a log-log adaptive ratio.

claims.result: Existing Pattern Censoring code has O_f(log log n) redundancy ratio on the stated counting-function regularly varying envelope family with index in [0,1).
claims.scope: Not fixed-factor or exact adaptation. Index-zero benchmark is asymptotically exact; positive-index comparison is only up to constants.

unresolved: The catalogue generic framework does not specify a class collection. These partials do not resolve exact or fixed-factor adaptation for the intended uncountable regularly varying envelope collection.
units: Authored proofs use natural logarithms (nats). The source uses base-2 logarithms (bits); division by ln 2 converts nats to bits without changing redundancy ratios.
evidence: RESEARCH.md, INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md, SOURCE_GATE.md; no numerical mathematical computation checks claimed.
